# Sandboxed project runs: mount the project and every repo, suite pages in containers ## What to build A project run (a multi-repo suite started in `/.projects//`) can run in a sandbox container, as a workspace run can today (spec goal **MR-08**, "A sandboxed project run mounts the project folder and every repo of the project, each at its path under `/workspaces`, so the `repos/` links resolve inside the container (`sandbox.ts:611` mounts one workspace today)"). graph-manager side: `Sandboxes.start` takes extra repo mounts; `POST /api/runs/project~` with `sandbox: true` and the resume of a sandboxed project suite start a container whose cwd is the project folder and whose command is `node suite --project . --provider

… --web-serve`; `Sandboxes.pageOf` and the stop route resolve `project~` records; the Start run drawer enables the sandbox switch for a project. Three small engine changes make a suite work in a container at all: the suite id honours `GRAPH_EXECUTION_RUN_ID` when it starts with `suite-` (graph-manager must know the id before the container starts: it names the container, keys the record and places the ready file), the suite page listens where `GRAPH_EXECUTION_WEB_HOST`/`_PORT` say and checks `GRAPH_EXECUTION_WEB_TOKEN` like a run page, and `suite.json` records `sandbox: { image }` (as `state.json` does) so a resume knows the suite ran in a sandbox. NOT in this task: the `graph-execution --sandbox` command from a terminal (`POST /api/internal/sandbox-runs`, routes/internal.ts:114–160) keeps answering `--sandbox works only for runs` for suites; Create PR (another task); anything about how the suite runs its features. ## What already exists (read, don't rebuild) - `src/server/runhome.ts`: `PROJECT_PREFIX = "project~"`, `type RunHome = { kind: "workspace"; id; path; workspace: Workspace } | { kind: "project"; id; path; project: Project }`, `resolveRunHome(workspacesDir, store, id)`, `workspaceHome(ws)`, `homeAsWorkspace(home)` (a project as `{ id: "project~", path: , rel: ".projects/", forge: "project", fullPath: }`), `projectRepos(workspacesDir, home)` → `{ name, path, workspace?: Workspace }[]` in project.json order. - `src/server/routes/runs.ts` `POST /api/runs/:ws`: for a project it builds args with `projectStartArgs({ provider, options })` = `["suite", "--project", ".", "--provider", p, …options, "--web"]` and currently answers 400 `sandboxed project runs are not supported yet` when `sandbox: true`. `src/server/routes/resume.ts` `resumeRun(ctx, home: RunHome, runId, opts)` resumes a project suite on the server with `["suite", "--resume", "--run", id, "--web"]` and answers 400 with the same message for a sandboxed one. The Start run drawer (`src/web/pages/StartRunDrawer.tsx`) disables the sandbox switch for `project~` ids with the hint `Sandboxed project runs are not available yet`. Remove all three refusals here. - `src/server/liverun.ts` `liveRunIn(ctx, { id, path })`; sandbox records of a project are keyed `project~/` with `workspace: "project~"`. - Engine: `suite.json` (`suite/state.ts`) has `project?`, `repos?`, per-feature `repo?`. The suite copies the reviewers file to `/reviewers.json` (`RUN_REVIEWERS_FILE`) and reads `GRAPH_EXECUTION_REVIEWERS`. ## Context: files to read before implementing - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox.ts` (96–108 `StartParams`; 116–119 `SANDBOX_REVIEWERS_FILE`; 499–682 `start`: 567–578 run dir/owner, 586–598 reviewers copy, 600–611 env and mounts, 612–625 body, 633–646 record; 688–706 `release`/`stop`; 765–792 `pageOf`, which resolves `r.workspace` with `resolveWorkspace` at line 770). - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox-run.ts` (233–264 `WorkspaceMount`, `workspaceMount`; 154–197 `sandboxEnv`, which sets `GRAPH_EXECUTION_RUN_ID`, `_WEB_HOST=0.0.0.0`, `_WEB_PORT=7600`, `_WEB_TOKEN`, `_READY_FILE`). - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox-paths.ts` (all, 75 lines: `containerRoot`, `toContainer`, `toHost`, `toContainerArgs`, `PATH_OPTIONS` line 10). - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/runs.ts` (112–127: the sandboxed run start to copy), `routes/resume.ts` (44–62: the sandboxed resume to copy). - Engine: `packages/graph-execution/src/suite/orchestrator.ts` (145–194 `startSuite`: id at line 157; 527–571 `serveSuite`: `web.json` written at line 552 without `host`); `packages/graph-execution/src/suite/server.ts` (99–102 `createSuiteServer`; 345–353 the Host/Origin check; 482–492 `server.listen(0, "127.0.0.1")`); `packages/graph-execution/src/web/start.ts` (lines 7–27 `listenFromEnv`); `packages/graph-execution/src/web/server.ts` (108–117 `WEB_TOKEN_HEADER`, `tokenMatches`; 524–527 Host + token check; 589–592 listen); `packages/graph-execution/src/runner/startup.ts` (59–62, 79: how a run honours `RUN_ID_ENV`); `packages/graph-execution/src/runner/run.ts` (~line 193: `sandbox: { image }` from `SANDBOX_ENV`/`SANDBOX_IMAGE_ENV`); `packages/graph-execution/src/suite/state.ts` (38–66 `suiteStateSchema`); `packages/graph-execution/src/web/webjson.ts`; `packages/graph-execution/src/suite/spawn.ts` (34–40: feature children get `{ ...process.env, ...env }` with `RUN_ID_ENV` overridden per feature). - Tests to copy from: `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/runs.sandbox.test.ts` (lines 1–112: fake Docker, `prepareTools`/`buildImages` mocks, the mount assertions), `src/server/sandbox-run.test.ts` (134–188 `workspaceMount`), `src/server/sandbox.test.ts` (75–127 win32 start; 219+ `pageOf`), `src/server/routes/resume.test.ts` (112–156 sandboxed resume), `packages/graph-execution/src/suite/server.test.ts`, `packages/graph-execution/src/web/start.test.ts` if present. ## Patterns to follow Current single mount (sandbox.ts:611): ```ts const mounts = [workspaceMount(p.ws, config.workspacesDir, this.self, config.sandboxWorkspacesSource, pf), tools, clis]; ``` `workspaceMount(ws, …)` already handles a `Workspace` whose `rel` is `.projects/` (volume `Subpath`, bind `path.posix.join(m.Source, ws.rel)`, override, win32 `/workspaces/`), so `homeAsWorkspace(home)` can be passed as `p.ws` unchanged. Run page listen + token (web/server.ts:524–527, 591), to copy into the suite server: ```ts const hosts = [`127.0.0.1:${port}`, `localhost:${port}`]; if (!hosts.includes(req.headers.host ?? "")) return void res.writeHead(421).end("Misdirected Request"); if (listen.token !== undefined && !tokenMatches(req.headers[WEB_TOKEN_HEADER], listen.token)) return void res.writeHead(401).end("Unauthorized"); … server.listen(listen.port, listen.host, resolve); ``` How a run takes its forced id (startup.ts:61–62): ```ts const forced = env[RUN_ID_ENV]; if (forced !== undefined && !RUN_ID_PATTERN.test(forced)) throw new UsageError(`invalid ${RUN_ID_ENV}: ${forced}`); ``` ## Step-by-step tasks ### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/src/suite/orchestrator.ts` - **IMPLEMENT**: in `startSuite` (line 157) use `process.env[RUN_ID_ENV]` (or an injected `env` option, default `process.env`) when it matches `RUN_ID_PATTERN` and starts with `suite-`; otherwise generate as today (a non-suite value, e.g. a run id inherited from a launcher, is ignored, never an error). If `/.graph-execution//suite.json` already exists → `UsageError(\`suite ${id} already exists\`)` (a folder holding only graph-manager's `.sandbox-reviewers.json` or `.ready.json` is fine: graph-manager creates it before the container starts). Record `sandbox: { image: process.env[SANDBOX_IMAGE_ENV] ?? "" }` in the new suite.json when `process.env[SANDBOX_ENV] === "1"`. In `serveSuite`, write `web.json` as `{ url, pid, host: os.hostname() }` (as `web/serve.ts:74` does), so graph-manager never takes a container pid for a host pid. - **GOTCHA**: feature runs get their own `RUN_ID_ENV` from `suite/spawn.ts` (line 302 of orchestrator passes it); make sure the suite's own forced id is not passed down unchanged anywhere else (e.g. the e2e/joint phase must not call `startup()` with it). - **VALIDATE**: `npm test -w graph-execution -- src/suite/orchestrator.test.ts` ### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/src/suite/state.ts` - **IMPLEMENT**: `sandbox: z.object({ image: z.string() }).optional()` on `suiteStateSchema` (an old suite.json still loads). ### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/src/suite/server.ts` - **IMPLEMENT**: `SuiteServerOptions.listen?: { host: string; port: number; token?: string }` (default `{ host: "127.0.0.1", port: 0 }`), `serveSuite` passes `listenFromEnv()` from `../web/start.js`. Listen on it; the page URL stays `http://127.0.0.1:/`; the Host check stays `127.0.0.1:`/`localhost:`; with a token every request needs `x-graph-execution-token` (import `WEB_TOKEN_HEADER` and reuse a constant-time compare like `web/server.ts:111–116`; export `tokenMatches` from there rather than copying it). - **GOTCHA**: another task edits `suite/server.ts` for the multi-repo suite page; keep this change to the options, the listen call and the request guard at the top of `handle`, so merges stay small. - **VALIDATE**: `npm test -w graph-execution -- src/suite/server.test.ts` ### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox-run.ts` and `sandbox-paths.ts` - **IMPLEMENT**: `repoMounts(home: Workspace /* homeAsWorkspace of the project */, repos: Workspace[], links: string[], workspacesDir, self, override, platform): WorkspaceMount[]` = `workspaceMount(repo, …)` for each repo (at its own `containerRoot`: the host path on Linux/macOS, `/workspaces/` on a Windows host), and **on a Windows host only** also the same source mounted at `${containerRoot(home, "win32")}/repos/` — the project's `repos/` entries are junctions with Windows targets that a Linux container cannot follow, so a nested mount puts the real checkout there. On Linux/macOS the symlinks point at the host paths where the repos are mounted, so they resolve without extra mounts. `sandbox-paths.ts`: add `"--project"` to `PATH_OPTIONS` (an absolute `--project` value is mapped on win32). - **GOTCHA**: on win32 Docker Desktop's behaviour for a mount target that is a junction inside another bind mount is not covered by CI (no Docker there); only the mount list is asserted. Say so in a code comment. - **VALIDATE**: `npm test -w graph-manager -- src/server/sandbox-run.test.ts` ### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox.ts` - **IMPLEMENT**: `StartParams.repos?: { link: string; workspace: Workspace }[]`; mounts = `[workspaceMount(p.ws…), ...repoMounts(...), tools, clis]`. Owner, git identity and win32 git config stay from `p.ws.path` (the project folder; `safe.directory=*` covers the repos). `pageOf` (line 770) resolves `r.workspace` with `resolveRunHome(config.workspacesDir, store, r.workspace)` and compares `path.join(home.path, RUNS_DIR, r.runId)`. `imageFor("project~")` already falls back to the global image (no `workspaceSettings` image/recipe for a project): keep it so. - **VALIDATE**: `npm test -w graph-manager -- src/server/sandbox.test.ts` ### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/runs.ts`, `routes/resume.ts`, web drawer - **IMPLEMENT**: project start with `sandbox: true`: `runId = \`suite-${newRunId()}\``, `ctx.sandboxes.start({ ws: homeAsWorkspace(home), cwd: home.path, args: args.filter((a) => a !== "--web"), runId, providers: [provider], repos })` with `repos` from `projectRepos` (a repo without its workspace → 409 `repo has no workspace`), then `rememberSandbox(ctx, home.id, true)`, save defaults, 201 `{ runId, viewUrl: viewUrlOf(home.id, runId) }`; `SandboxError` → `{ error, output? }` as lines 118–123. Resume of a project suite is sandboxed when `opts.sandbox`, `suite.json.sandbox` is set, or `ctx.sandboxes?.recordOf(home.id, runId)`: `release`, take the lock host (`readLock(runDir)`, as resume.ts:49–51), `start({ …, args: ["suite", "--resume", "--run", runId], image: suite.sandbox?.image, takeLockFrom })`. Drop the drawer's project-sandbox refusal and its hint (the image hint reads `its own container, sees the project and its repos`). - **GOTCHA**: the reviewers copy goes to `/.sandbox-reviewers.json` (sandbox.ts:592 uses `runDir` = `/.graph-execution/`, which is the suite dir here: nothing to change). A resume reads `/reviewers.json` (`RUN_REVIEWERS_FILE`), which the suite wrote: also unchanged. - **VALIDATE**: `npm test -w graph-manager -- src/server/routes/runs.sandbox.test.ts src/server/routes/resume.test.ts src/web/pages/StartRunDrawer.test.tsx` ### Tests to add - `packages/graph-execution/src/suite/orchestrator.test.ts` (or a new `suite/runid.test.ts`): with `GRAPH_EXECUTION_RUN_ID=suite-gm-x` the suite folder is `.graph-execution/suite-gm-x`; with `gm-x` (no `suite-` prefix) a generated id is used; an existing `suite-gm-x/suite.json` → UsageError; `SANDBOX_ENV=1` + `SANDBOX_IMAGE_ENV=img:1` → `suite.json.sandbox = { image: "img:1" }`. - `packages/graph-execution/src/suite/server.test.ts`: `createSuiteServer({ …, listen: { host: "127.0.0.1", port: 0, token: "s3cret" } })` answers 401 without the header and 200 with it; the URL is `http://127.0.0.1:/`. - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox-run.test.ts`: `repoMounts` on linux (each repo at its own path, no nested mount), win32 (`/workspaces/github/acme/api` and `/workspaces/.projects/billing/repos/api`), with a volume self-mount (`Subpath` = each repo's `rel`). - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/runs.sandbox.test.ts` new case "starts a project run in its own container": project fixture as in the task-9 tests (two git workspaces `github~acme~api`/`github~acme~web`, `/.projects/billing` with `git init`, `project.json`, `repos/` links via `symlink(target, link, process.platform === "win32" ? "junction" : "dir")`, the store's `projects.billing` record). POST `/api/runs/project~billing { provider: "fake", sandbox: true }` → 201, `runId` matches `/^suite-gm-\d{8}-\d{6}-[0-9a-f]{4}$/`; the container's `Cmd` ends with `suite --project . --provider fake --web-serve`, `WorkingDir` = `toContainer(homeWs, projDir)`, `Labels["gm.workspace"] = "project~billing"`, `Env` contains `GRAPH_EXECUTION_RUN_ID=`, `HostConfig.Mounts` = project mount, api mount, web mount (plus the two nested mounts when `process.platform === "win32"`), tools, clis; the store holds `sandboxes["project~billing/"]`; `GET /api/runs?workspace=project~billing` shows the run with `sandbox: { running: true }` once `suite.json` exists (write one by hand in the suite dir, as in the task-9 fixture). - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox.test.ts`: `pageOf(/.graph-execution/)` finds a `project~billing` record. - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/resume.test.ts`: a project suite with `suite.json.sandbox = { image: "img:old" }`, status `failed` → resume starts a container with `["suite", "--resume", "--run", ]` and image `img:old`. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] A sandboxed project run's container mounts the project folder and every repo of the project at its `/workspaces` path (its host path off Windows), and on a Windows host also each repo under `repos/` of the project mount; tools and CLIs as before. - [ ] The suite in the container uses the id graph-manager chose, listens on `0.0.0.0:7600` with the token, and its page is reachable through `/runs/project~//view/`. - [ ] `suite.json` of a suite started in a sandbox has `sandbox.image`; resume of it starts a new container with that image. - [ ] Without the env variables, a suite behaves exactly as before (generated id, 127.0.0.1, no token); all existing suite tests pass. - [ ] The Start run drawer offers Run in sandbox for a project. ## Validation commands ```bash npm run typecheck && npm run lint npm test -w graph-execution -- src/suite npm test -w graph-manager -- src/server/sandbox-run.test.ts src/server/sandbox.test.ts src/server/routes/runs.sandbox.test.ts src/server/routes/resume.test.ts src/web/pages/StartRunDrawer.test.tsx ```
